name: NCP349MNBKTBG
title: NCP349: positive overvoltage protection controller with internal 65 mΩ NMOS switch, DFN6 1.6 × 2 mm
summary: A series switch for a charger or system input that passes the supply through an on-chip N-channel MOSFET (65 mΩ typ, gate driven by an internal charge pump) only while the input sits between an undervoltage and an overvoltage threshold. The input withstands 30 V and is protected against overvoltage up to 28 V; above OVLO the output is cut off within 5 µs max, and outside the window an open-drain FLAG output goes low. An active-low EN input turns the switch off without affecting fault detection. Five threshold versions are offered; NCP349MNBKTBG has UVLO 3.25 V typ and OVLO 6.4 V typ with 55 ms start-up delay.

Other UVLO and OVLO thresholds can be manufactured; availability through onsemi.
Package marking: two-letter device code XX, date code M, and a Pb-free indicator (G or microdot).

pins.name: IN
pins.function: Supply input from the adapter or USB bus. Pin 7 is the exposed pad, tied inside to the switch drain; pins 1 and 7 are joined on the board. Bypass to GND with a low-ESR ceramic of 1 µF or more placed close to the chip.

pins.name: FLAG
pins.function: Active-low fault report: pulled low while the input is above OVLO or below UVLO. Needs an external pull-up of at least 10 kΩ to the logic supply.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Switched output; follows IN when no fault is present. Both OUT pins are joined on the board.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Active-low enable. High puts the part in shutdown with OUT cut off from IN; low (grounded, pulled down or driven by an I/O) allows normal operation. Has no effect on fault detection.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: The NCP349 sits between a wall adapter or USB input and a CC/CV charger or system. A 1 µF capacitor bypasses the input to ground. Both IN pins (1 and the exposed pad 7) take the input and both OUT pins (4, 5) feed the charger, which charges the battery. EN is held or driven low by a microprocessor to enable the switch. FLAG is pulled up through 10 kΩ to VBat and read by the microprocessor as the fault signal.

equations.name: Output voltage under load
equations.note: With Rload = 8.0 Ω, Vin = 5.0 V and RDS(on) = 65 mΩ: Iout = 618 mA, Vout = 8 × 0.618 = 4.95 V.

operation.text: An internal low-resistance NMOS switch joins IN to OUT. With EN low and UVLO < Vin < OVLO the switch is on and OUT follows IN less the RDS(on) drop. If Vin goes above OVLO or below UVLO, or EN goes high, the switch opens. The part guards against positive overvoltage up to 28 V.

With EN low, once Vin rises past UVLO an internal timer runs for ton and the output then ramps up under soft-start. FLAG goes high a further tstart after the output reaches 0.3 V. ton and tstart depend on the version: 1.8 ms and 1.2 ms typ for NCP349MN, 10 ms for NCP349MNAE, 55 ms for NCP349MNBG, NCP349MNBK and NCP349MNAM.

At power-up OUT is off, FLAG low and the timer reset. While Vin is outside the UVLO-OVLO window OUT stays off, FLAG low and the timer counts again from zero once Vin returns inside. Inside the window the timer runs to ton; Vin is checked again, then EN: EN = 1 leaves OUT open, EN = 0 closes the switch (Vout = Vin). After a second timer period FLAG goes high, with OUT open or closed according to EN. Vin is then watched continuously; leaving the window takes FLAG low and OUT open, and the sequence restarts.
On a rising input the output stays off until Vin passes UVLO plus its hysteresis. FLAG is held low while Vin is below UVLO. The hysteresis gives noise immunity against transients.
While Vin is above OVLO the switch stays open and FLAG is held low; the output is cut off within toff (1.5 µs typ) of the crossing. The threshold has hysteresis for noise immunity.

Open-drain, active low: it pulls low as soon as Vin exceeds OVLO or falls below UVLO, and is released tstart after the output becomes available once Vin is back in range. It needs a pull-up to Vbat of typically 1 MΩ and at least 10 kΩ; Vbat must be at least 2.5 V. FLAG always reports the input state, even with the switch turned off by EN = 1.

Drive EN low or ground it for normal operation. A high level opens the switch, disconnecting OUT from IN, within tdis (1.0 µs typ). A lockout fault wins over EN: the switch stays open while one is present.
The on-chip N-channel switch, gate driven from an internal charge pump, protects the load on OUT from positive overvoltage; its RDS(on) of 65 mΩ typ sets the conduction loss in normal operation.
The IN pin meets IEC 61000-4-2 level 4, ±15 kV air and ±8.0 kV contact discharge, provided at least 1.0 µF is connected from Vin to GND close to the part.

The switch is a 2 A rated NMOSFET, and its heat leaves through the board. The exposed pad (pin 7) is the switch drain, internally on the input; it joins pin 1 and its copper spreads the heat. The pad connects to no other potential. RθJA falls from about 185 °C/W at 50 mm² of copper to about 98 °C/W at 600 mm² with 1 oz copper, and from about 160 °C/W to about 82 °C/W with 2 oz copper.
